Appearance:
 Shri Anil Khare, Senior Advocate with Shri Ashley Johnm
 and Shri Sanjay Verma, Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Satya Pal Chadar- G.A. for the State.

Mr. Sandeep Kumar Sen, learned counsel for the objector
 Order

This is first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 439 of Cr.P.C.).
2.

The applicant is in custody since 07.08.2024 in connection with Crime No.16/2024 registered at P.S.- STF, District Bhopal, (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 468, 471, 255,
260 and 120-B of IPC.

3. Prosecution story, in brief, is that present applicant Anubhav Dubey, during his posting in Bandhan Bank as well as Axis Bank got executed forged sale-deeds and on the basis of forged sale-deeds, got sanctioned loans from India Shelter Bank/Bandhan Bank/Axis Bank.
4. Learned senior counsel for the applicant submits that after investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Applicant is in jail since 07.08.2024.
In the instant case, one Sandeep Choubey is kingpin/mastermind of the whole scam.
It is also urged that earlier applicant used to work as employee in Bandhan NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:60902 2 MCRC-49526-2024 Bank/Axis Bank.

There is no evidence on record to show that it is applicant, who opened fictitious Anubhav Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77114787/
1 accounts in Bandhan Bank/Axis Bank.

sentences.text: It is also urged that the persons in whose name fictitious accounts have been opened have not been made accused/witness in the case.
It is also urged that there is no document to show that applicant opened any account in Jana Bank or sanctioned/got sanctioned loan.
Further, no application form for opening of account by present applicant or that he has sanctioned the loan is on record.

5. Learned senior counsel for the applicant after referring to statement of Devesh Soni submits that at relevant point of time, Devesh Soni was posted in Axis Bank and it was his duty to open the accounts.
It is also urged that one fictitious account was opened in the name of Aarti Jain in Axis Bank by using ID of prosecution witness Devesh Soni.
Statement of this Aarti Jain has not been recorded.
Above account of Aarti Jain has not been opened by present applicant.

6. Learned Senior counsel for the applicant after referring to Ankur's Jain statement submits that in Axis Bank, fictitious account was opened in the name of Rajul Samdariya but statement of Rajul Samdariya is not on record.
There is no evidence on record to show that on application form,
signature
is not of Rajul Samdariya.
It is not established that it is the present applicant, who opened fictitious account in the name of Rajul Samdariya in Axis Bank.
It is also urged that STF has written letter to India Shelter Housing Finance Limited (India Shelter Finance Corporation) but no reply has been received by the STF of aforesaid letter.

It is also urged that initially, present case was registered on the basis of written complaints submitted by one Sumit and in written application,
One Hinduja Housing Finance Company is mentioned.

There is nothing on record to show that applicant has any connection with aforesaid Hinduja Housing Finance NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:60902 3 MCRC-49526-2024 Company.

sentences.text: Applicant did not get open any account in Madhya Pradesh Gramin Bank.
In aforesaid written complaint, primarily allegations are against Vikash Tiwari and his syndicate that they forged documents etc. and got loans sanctioned.

7. Learned senior counsel for the applicant further submits that it is correct that present applicant has taken loan of Rs.16,74,000/-from India Shelter Housing Finance Limited (India Shelter Finance Corporation) but it is also urged that it is the applicant himself, who has been cheated.

entities.text: India Shelter Housing Finance Limited (India Shelter Finance Corporation)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further, it is also urged that applicant has deposited installment of Rs.5 Lacs, which shows applicant's bona fide.
If applicant has forged documents and fraudulently got loan sanctioned, then, he would not have deposited any installment, leave alone Rs.5,00,000/-.
There is nothing on record to show that present applicant forged sale-deeds of plot owned by Sumit Kale and Nitesh.
Relevant forged sale-deed has not been sent for examination to handwriting expert.
Thus, there is no report of handwriting expert on record.

As it is not proved that applicant forged sale deed, therefore,
applicant cannot be charged under Sections 467 and 468 of IPC.
In this connection, learned senior counsel for the applicant has relied upon Sheila Sebastian Vs. R.Jawaharaj, AIR 2018 SC 2434.

sentences.text: After referring to statement of Krishna Vishwakarma, it is urged that other persons are also involved in the case.

8. Learned senior counsel for the applicant further submits that so far as Jana Bank is concerned, it has been alleged that on the basis of sale deed executed by Sajjan, loan has been sanctioned but with respect to above, no document has been filed in the case.
No amount has been credited into the account of present applicant.

It is also urged that applicant is ready to deposit remaining amount Anubhav Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77114787/
2 out of Rs.16,74,000/- under protest.

entities.text: Anubhav Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also urged that in the instant case, no complaint has been lodged by India Shelter Housing Finance Limited.

In the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:60902 4 MCRC-49526-2024 instant case, there are no sale-deeds on record.
On above grounds, it has been prayed that the applicant be released on bail pending the trial.

9. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail and submits that the present applicant has sanctioned the loan on the basis of forged sale-deeds, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.
10. This Court has examined the submissions of learned counsel for the parties in the light of documents available on record.

After examining the same and having regard to the evidence available on record, at this stage (especially, memorandum of applicant as well as co-accused Sandeep and Puneet @ Rahul as well as recovery from Krishna Vishwakarma, statements of Krishna Vishwakarma, Devesh Soni, Ankur Jain and Rajjan etc.) and also the fact that investigation is continuing under Section 178(3) of Cr.P.C., this Court does not deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
11.
Accordingly, this application is dismissed.
